title: Continue a shop display's product pattern
instruction: Fill the two empty spots on the display so it continues the same pattern.
context: Shops lay shelves out to a planogram, and staff restocking a display must continue its arrangement. The robot has to infer the repeating sequence from the display itself; the stock is shuffled so the item in front of each gap is the wrong one.
setup: A wooden display shelf (66 x 11 cm) runs left to right 33 cm in front of the arm bases, with a white back panel carrying a red sign and a yellow price strip in front. Its seven spots, 9 cm apart, hold from the robot's left: soup can, ketchup bottle, green beans can, soup can, ketchup bottle, then two empty spots. On a cardboard mat 15 cm in front of the bases stand, left to right: ketchup, yogurt cup, soup can, mustard, green beans can.
scoring: 0 if any product ever tips past 45 degrees or a display product is ever moved more than 2 cm. Otherwise 0.5 for each empty spot holding the product that continues the pattern (sixth: green beans can, seventh: soup can), upright within 15 degrees and centred within 3 cm of the spot.
reset_notes: Return the display products and stock to their marks, leaving the last two spots empty.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only; the products are solid models of real groceries (cans 6.8 cm wide, bottles 17 cm tall). Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2). The shelf, back panel, sign and mat are fixed.
